answer: Because the wharf audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. A farm thus spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the trellis quota and the vault admission check. Admission is capped at 4 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. That is 35 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
